inputs.proposal: Bridge cleanup after the coalescing change: setSignalSet takes an opaque pointer, signal decode reads the standard 8-byte CAN payload, the staging buffer is rebuilt per frame, and dropped frames are reported from the GUI-side frame handler.
inputs.original_proposal: Bridge cleanup after the coalescing change: setSignalSet takes an opaque pointer, signal decode reads the standard 8-byte CAN payload, the staging buffer is rebuilt per frame, and dropped frames are reported from the GUI-side frame handler.

blockers: claim: C ABI integrity violation: setSignalSet takes an opaque pointer but the implementation assumes the opaque pointer points to a C++ type (QttuneSignalSet) which is defined in the C++ header 'qttune/signals.h'. An opaque pointer at the C boundary should point to a POD struct defined in the C interface, not a C++ type.; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: const QttuneSignalSet* sigSet = static_cast<const QttuneSignalSet*>(set);

claim: Buffer size assumption violation: signal decoding uses hardcoded 8-byte length instead of actual payload length, breaking CAN-FD (64+ byte) support and contradicting the stated fix.; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: if (qttune_decode_signal(&def, frame->data, 8, &val) == 0) {

claim: Thread safety violation: m_stagingBuffer is modified in handleFrameInternal without any synchronization, but is read by the coalescing timer callback on the GUI thread - classic data race.; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: m_stagingBuffer.clear();

claim: Lost drop notification: the notifyDropped() method was removed and the drop counting logic is broken - m_lastReportedDropped is never updated, causing the drop count to never be reported to the GUI.; file: app/qttunebridge.cpp; quote: if (dropped != m_lastReportedDropped) {
questions: What is the ownership model for the QttuneSignalSet passed to setSignalSet? Who allocates it and who frees it?
Why was the proper drop notification mechanism removed instead of fixing it?
What is the intended coalescing window and how does clear-and-refill differ from the merge approach in terms of signal semantics?

claim: Header includes removed breaking C++ type access: the #include for "qttune/signals.h" was removed from the header, making QttuneSignalSet undefined and breaking the static_cast in the implementation.; file: app/qttunebridge.h; quote: #include "qttune/signals.h"
nits: The comment about 'one contiguous range instead of per-row notifications' is now incorrect since the code still emits a single dataChanged signal, which is good, but the comment should match the implementation.
The staging buffer should probably be a member of the SignalListModel rather than QtTuneBridge for better encapsulation.
